text.p: BEC Group Inc's acquisition of Holding B.F., the French holding company that owns Bolle France, will add about $30 to $40 million to annual revenues and be accretive to shareholders immediately, BEC chief executive Martin Franklin said in an interview Thursday.
BEC posted $623,000 operating income on revenues of $16.0 million in the first quarter, compared with a $1.0 million operating income on revenues of 17.0 million a year ago.

The holding company of Bolle Inc and ORC Technologies said Thursday it completed the Bolle France acquisition, first announced on June 5, for $53 million, including about $31 million in cash; $9.3 million of BEC preferred stock; $10.8 million in preferred Bolle Inc common stock; and five percent of Bolle Inc's common stock.
Holding B.F. shareholders also received warrants to buy about 10 percent of Bolle Inc's common stock at $3.10 a share. The warrants are exercisable in three years.
Franklin said he wants to split BEC Group into two seperate companies -- Bolle Inc and ORC Technologies -- to boost shareholder value.
Franklin added he thought BEC shares, which traded at 4-11/16 Thursday afternoon, up 7/16, were undervalued.
"If you were to assume Bolle is worth $3.10 (the warrants' exercise price), that only leaves about $1.50 a share for ORC Technologies," Franklin said. "We believe ORC is worth substantially more."
Franklin declined to say when the company plans to split the group saying, only it could be within months.
